title: Heat-health operations
summary: For high-heat conditions, operational plans should prioritize access to cooler environments, shade, hydration and rapid escalation for people showing signs of heat stress.

title: Hydration and exposure reduction
summary: Heat plans for gatherings should reduce prolonged exposure and ensure practical access to drinking water and cooling opportunities.

title: Forecast-to-action principle
summary: An effective warning system should connect forecasts to timely, understandable and actionable decisions rather than stopping at hazard prediction.

title: Last-mile warning delivery
summary: Warnings are most useful when they reach the people responsible for acting and are translated into concrete instructions appropriate to each audience.

title: European heat-stress context
summary: European climate monitoring shows increasing exposure to strong heat stress, making local adaptation and preparedness increasingly important.

title: Official warning context
summary: Official warnings from national meteorological services provide authoritative hazard context; operational risk still depends on local exposure and resources.

title: Capacity-gap reasoning
summary: Resource demand should be compared with available throughput during the critical window; the largest feasible capacity gap is a priority intervention candidate.

title: Schedule-shift reasoning
summary: Activities involving more heat-sensitive groups can be shifted outside the peak environmental window when this preserves event continuity and reduces exposure.

title: Response coverage
summary: Response coverage should increase when high crowd exposure and environmental risk overlap, while access routes remain clear.

title: Uncertainty-aware planning
summary: Operational decisions should consider expected, lower and upper risk cases rather than relying on a single precise forecast value.
